column2: You can let something pass without deciding what to think of it.
When something outside you hurts, notice the judgment you have added to it.
The thoughts you return to help shape the life you experience.
Spend less time debating what a good person is. Practise being one.
You do not have to become like the person who hurt you.
The mind takes on the colors of the thoughts it lives with.
You can return to the quiet within you whenever you need to.
Give the thing in front of you your full attention.
Some things are yours to influence. Some things are not.
Notice the difference between what happened and the meaning you gave it.
Let the day be as it is, even when it is not the day you planned.
Ask what you have within you that could help you meet this moment.
Learning sometimes means being willing to look like a beginner.
Someone else's words need not decide what you believe about yourself.
You may not choose every part of your story. You can choose how you meet it.
What has left your life can be thought of as returned, not only lost.
Sometimes the things we imagine are harder to bear than what is here.
Having enough is not only about having more. It is also about wanting less.
Life is happening while we wait for the right time to begin.
Let today be a small, complete life of its own.
Spend time with people who help you become more yourself.
Difficulty can reveal strengths you have not needed to use before.
Courage makes a little more room for freedom.
When anger arrives, give yourself a little time before acting.
There is value in learning how to belong to yourself.
Living is something we keep learning by doing.
A life's value is not only in its length, but in how its days are lived.
Wisdom can make room for an ordinary, lasting cheerfulness.
Worry about endings can take us away from the life we have now.
Other people's words can help us discover what we mean.
Certainty can be strongest where understanding is still small.
Learning to live simply and well is a lifelong practice.
What we long for is part of what makes us human.
Understanding a feeling can change the way it holds you.
Hope and fear often arrive together.
Hostility can grow when it is returned. Care can interrupt it.
A feeling may loosen when another, stronger feeling has room to grow.
Freedom turns our attention toward living.
A good life is not only a reward to reach. It is a way to live now.
Sometimes wanting a thing comes before the reasons we give for wanting it.
Time alone can give you room to be fully yourself.
Learning to enjoy your own company can feel like freedom.
What we can see is not the whole of what is there.
Fitting in can cost us parts of ourselves. Notice what you want to keep.
We sometimes understand a thing's value only after it is gone.
Time can be more than something to get through. It can be something to use well.
You do not choose every card. You still have a hand to play.
What you carry within you matters more than what you own.
In resisting what harms you, take care of the person you are becoming.
What you give your attention to can begin to shape you.
Love does not always fit neatly inside our judgments.
Sometimes we are attached to the wanting as much as to the thing we want.
A belief shared by many people still deserves to be questioned.
There is a kind of maturity in recovering the wholeheartedness of play.
Even self-criticism contains a part of you that cares how you live.
The judgments we place on events are not the events themselves.
What you give your attention to becomes part of your experience.
Each time your attention wanders, bringing it back is part of the practice.
Small habits help hold a life together.
Part of wisdom is knowing what does not need your attention.
Being seen and appreciated matters to us.
Believing that life holds something worthwhile can help you find it.
A small worthwhile effort can keep your capacity for effort alive.
The things we do each day become the life we are making.
There can be something to learn in a quiet moment with yourself.
The heart has reasons that do not always fit into an explanation.
Notice how often the mind leaves the moment you are actually in.
We can be fragile and still have the capacity to reflect and understand.
What we repeat can begin to feel like who we are.
Our capacity to think is part of our dignity.
Power needs fairness, and fairness needs the means to act.
How we share a truth can help someone make room to hear it.
